instructions: docs/uashmc-design-guidelines.md (pitch-kit repo, source of truth for tokens.css)

typography.display: Source Serif 4, Georgia, Times New Roman, serif — h1/h2/h3 only
typography.ui: Be Vietnam Pro, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif — everything else

spacing.grid: strict 4px scale, tokens --space-1 (4px) through --space-10 (80px), no off-scale values

motion.reducedMotion: all duration tokens resolve to 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion; transform-based effects must still branch explicitly

design.density: comfortable — 44px minimum interactive target height, 4px baseline grid, generous spacing (not compact/dashboard-dense)

patterns: server-rendered content, client-side <script> filters over already-real HTML (no client-side data fetching/generation)
provenance data-src attribute carried as build-time metadata only — NOT visually styled on the public site (unlike the pitch-kit prototype's colour-coded demo overlay)

must: Reference tokens.css custom properties only — no raw hex/px/ms values in new CSS
16px body-copy floor; type scale in rem so it honours the reader's browser font-size setting
44px minimum height on interactive targets (buttons, inputs, filter chips) — audience skews senior/PWD
Filtering must stay a progressive enhancement over real server-rendered HTML — never hide content behind client-side-only rendering
Empty state must always explain WHY (which filter emptied it) and offer a phone/Viber fallback — never a bare 'no results'
prefers-reduced-motion must be honoured for any transform-based interaction
Never fabricate doctor facts (specialty/clinic day/room/HMO) — unverified fields render an explicit 'to confirm' placeholder, never a guess
[data-src] provenance attribute stays visually unstyled on this public build
avoid: shadcn default Button/Input/Select primitives — this project has its own .btn/.field system
Dark mode / color-scheme branching — the site is fixed light
Client-side-only doctor data (breaks crawlability + the no-JS baseline)
Any card grid that reads as generic SaaS (guidelines explicitly reject the 'identical icon card grid' pattern elsewhere in this project)

decisions.chosen: C, with A's doctor-card anatomy (small square photo + text row, not C's large 4:3 editorial card) and A's click-to-filter specialty tiles (tiles isolate a section instead of just scrolling to it)
decisions.rationale: With only 4 published doctors across 2 of 6 clinics, a flat filter bar mostly returns nothing (the pitch-kit's own documented finding). Sectioning by specialty plus an explicit 'not yet published' list turns that gap into upfront content instead of a dead end reached after filtering.
decisions.notConsistent: Day/HMO filtering from A and B was dropped — kept to name-search + specialty tiles only, to stay in line with C's minimalism rationale. Easy to add back if the roster grows.
decisions.abandonedVariants: explore-a-guided.astro, explore-b-faceted.astro, explore-c-sections.astro, explore.astro — removed after implementation; this decision record is the surviving trace.

decisions.note: 21st AI's free daily 'generate' quota was exhausted before any sketch ran, so these 3 were hand-drafted (not AI-generated) against the same tokens/real content.
decisions.chosen: C — Diagnostics / Surgery / Maternity tabs, mirroring services/index.astro's own CATEGORY_ORDER. 'Emergency and online' has no featured item so it has no tab.
decisions.rationale: Foreshadows the full category grid immediately below it instead of introducing an unrelated flat list of 4 — the highlight section and the full grid read as one system.
decisions.notConsistent: Recommendation had been B (Package Spotlight, since Maternity is the only service with a real price table) — user picked C instead. Maternity's price table is still shown in full inside its tab panel, so that content isn't lost, just not visually spotlighted.
decisions.abandonedVariants: explore-a-strip.astro, explore-b-spotlight.astro, explore-c-tabs.astro, explore.astro — removed after implementation; this decision record is the surviving trace.
